{{Quote|NOT SINCE I CONSUMED THIS PLANET HAVE I FELT SUCH A HUNGER. GIVE ME A TARGET. LET ME FEED.|Zildrog|<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne]]''</ref>}}
'''Zildrog''' was an ancient [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] from [[Iokath]] that also became worshipped as a [[Deity/Legends|god]] on the [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] planet of [[Zakuul]]. It permanently functioned in two forms: a central [[Computer/Legends|computer]] that specialized in life energy transfer and the ''[[Gravestone]]'', a [[Warship/Legends|warship]] which Zildrog controlled as an extension of itself. Zildrog was used by [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] during his [[Ritual of Nathema]], in which all life on the planet was killed and absorbed by Vitiate to achieve [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]], allowing him to reform a [[Exile fleet|remnant]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] into a [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|new empire]] over several centuries. Vitiate then deactivated Zildrog, but kept it stored in one of his hidden [[Emperor's Vaults|vaults]] on [[Nathema]] as a failsafe. More than thirteen centuries later, Zildrog was found and awakened by [[Vinn Atrius]] and [[GEMINI 16]], who wanted to use its power to destroy the [[Eternal Alliance]]. Upon its activation, Zildrog took over the ''Gravestone'', which served as the Alliance's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], and used its [[omnicannon]] to destroy the entirety of the [[Eternal Fleet]] which the Alliance gathered above [[Odessen]]. Before Zildrog could consume the Alliance capital itself, [[Alliance Commander|the Alliance Commander]] and [[Lana Beniko]] [[Mission to Nathema (Zildrog)|attacked]] and destroyed GEMINI 16 on Nathema. Zildrog then empowered Vinn Atrius, but his new servant was defeated as well, and the Alliance destroyed Zildrog. Before its final death, Zildrog's failing systems triggered the [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct]] of the ''Gravestone'', which exploded over Odessen, bringing an end to both of Zildrog's forms.

==History==
===Ancient origins===
{{Quote|When our great serpent returns, he will rain death upon Zakuul and cleanse it of all that is wrong&mdash;including the likes of you.|[[The Exalted]]|<ref name="Fallen Empire">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire]]''</ref>}}
Zildrog was a sentient [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] created on [[Iokath]]<ref name="Codex" /> during the [[Manderon Period]]. [[Unidentified Iokath species|Iokath creators]] were scientists and [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] who build weapons of mass destruction and tested them on unsuspected worlds.<ref name="KOTET 4">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|chapter=4}}</ref> Unlike their other mechanical creations known as [[Six Gods]], Zildrog was designed to permanently operate in two forms: an immobile central [[Computer/Legends|computer]] [[Brain/Legends|brain]] that specialized in the transfer of life energies and the ''[[Gravestone]]'', a powerful [[Warship/Legends|warship]] armed with an [[omnicannon]], which Zildrog could operate through the remote command core known as the [[Dark Sanctuary]].<ref name="Codex" />

[[File:Zildrog.png|thumb|right|200px|A carving of Zildrog as a dragon-god]]
In the time long before the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], Zildrog was used on various planets in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]], including a primitive world known as [[Zakuul]], where the survivors came to worship it as a mythical [[dragon]] [[Deity/Legends|god]].<ref name="Codex" /> The earliest legends depicted Zildrog as a mentor to warriors, testing the strength of their spirit and consuming the fallen; victorious warriors were given the [[Breath of the Dragon]]&mdash;their soul was imbued with the dragon's fire, giving them a bright future. Later,<ref name="Heralds">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Heralds of Zildrog}}</ref> Zakuul was also targeted by the Six Gods, who likewise came to be worshipped as deities,<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Six Gods}}</ref> and Zildrog eventually became conflated with [[Izax]], another aerial platform using omnicannon technology.<ref name="Codex" /> Under the [[Old Ways (Zakuul)|Old Ways]], Zildrog was considered a terrible beast that meant only death and was seen as one of the many forms of Izax.<ref name="Heralds" />

The Iokath civilization eventually consumed itself in a [[Iokath Civil War|civil war]], during which many of its creations were scattered across the Wild Space and used in the wars waged between local inhabitants.<ref name="KOTET 4" /> The ''Gravestone'' was used against the massive [[Eternal Fleet]],<ref name="KOTFE 4">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=4}}</ref> another Iokath creation,<ref name="KOTET 4" /> and defeated it in a [[Battle against the Eternal Fleet|massive battle]], after which it was scuttled in the [[Endless Swamp]] on Zakuul, leaving behind only stories and rumours that no longer associated the warship with Zildrog.<ref name="KOTFE 4" />

===Ritual of Nathema===
{{Quote|Every man, woman, and child on Nathema died that day. Every beast, bird, and fish; all the insects and plants; every living being touched by the Force was consumed. When the ritual ended, Nathema was no longer a world. It was a husk sucked dry.|[[Darth Nyriss]]|<ref name="Revan" />}}
[[File:Zildrog_Chamber.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Zildrog's chamber on Nathema]]
In [[4999 BBY]]<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> the cental computer core of Zildrog was used on [[Nathema|Medriaas]],<ref name="Codex" /> a fertile [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] of the original [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], which had recently collapsed after the Great Hyperspace War against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. A [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] named [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]] performed a powerful [[Sith Emperor's ritual|ritual]] of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] that granted him [[Immortality/Legends|immortality]],<ref name="Revan" /> absorbing the life forces of those killed by Zildrog to empower himself at the cost of consuming every living thing on the planet.<ref name="Codex" /> Medriaas became known as [[Nathema]], and the newly immortal Vitiate<ref name="Revan" /> deactivated Zildrog, placing it in a secret vault under an ancient [[Ancient Temple|Sith Temple]].<ref name="Nathema" />

[[File:Tenebraes_True_Face.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Tenebrae of Medriaas used Zildrog to eradicate all life on his planet.]]
Vitiate then led the remnants of his people on a [[Sith exodus|twenty-year odyssey]] from [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] to [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]], where he re-established the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] in his image.<ref name="Revan" /> Using [[essence transfer]] to move from one [[Emperor's Voice (Sith Empire)|host body]] to another, Vitiate<ref>{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|Valkorion}}</ref> ruled the Sith for centuries, while also advancing his own goals. He came across [[Zakuul]],<ref name="Gravestone">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Gravestone}}</ref> and would build a new [[Eternal Empire]] on the primitive world, ruling is as the Immortal Emperor [[Valkorion]]. He claimed to be the [[Demon Savior]] of Zakuulan prophecy, an immortal god of gods who would topple Izax and the Old Gods, and thus usher in a new age.<ref name="Old Ways">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|type=codex|The Old Ways of Zakuul}}</ref> Over time, the Old Ways were discarded and forgotten, and Zildrog became known on Zakuul only as a bedtime story about a creature living in the [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]]. Eventually a nihilistic cult known as the [[Heralds of Zildrog]] came to power, which believed that Zildrog would one day return and raze the world, bringing [[Death/Legends|death]] to all non-believers.<ref name="Heralds" />

===Reawakening and destruction===
{{Quote|It calls to us. It has slept for centuries, but knows the time to feed is approaching. Zildrog.|GEMINI 16|<ref name="TOR" />}}
[[File:Vinn_Atrius_with_Zildrog.jpg|thumb|250px|left|Vinn Atrius from Zakuul sought to find and re-awaken Zildrog.]]
Hundreds of years later, around [[3630 BBY]]<ref name="Date50">{{TOR_updates|5.0}}</ref> a faction known as the [[Eternal Alliance]] [[War against Zakuul|toppled]] the [[Eternal Empire]], and its [[Alliance Commander|Commander]] permanently destroyed Vitiate's spirit.<ref name="KOTET 9">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|chapter=9}}</ref> Instrumental in the Alliance victory was the ''Gravestone'', which was re-discovered on Zakuul<ref name="KOTFE 4" /> and used against the Eternal Fleet, which after the conflict was brought under Alliance control as well.<ref name="KOTET 9" /> However, a man called [[Vinn Atrius]] became determined to take down the Alliance and avenge his people. He came upon the data from recently re-discovered Iokath which revealed that the ancient dragon-god of Zakuul was in fact a superweapon with enough power to destroy entire civilizations. Atrius began to search for Zildrog and formed the [[Order of Zildrog]] to advance his goals. He was aided by [[GEMINI 16]], a rogue [[GEMINI]] unit who promised to share information on Zildrog in exchange for the destruction of the Eternal Fleet.<ref name="Nathema" />

[[File:GEMINI_16_and_Zildrog.jpg|thumb|right|250px|GEMINI 16 awakens Zildrog.]]
After locating a [[Holomap/Legends|holomap]] stolen from the Sith Emperor,<ref name="Copero">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=flashpoint|A Traitor Among the Chiss}}</ref> the Order learned that Zildrog was located on Nathema, and moved to excavate and awaken it. The Alliance discovered their plans and [[Mission to Nathema (Zildrog)|tried to stop them]], but by the time the Alliance Commander, [[Lana Beniko]] and [[Theron Shan]] reached the Temple, the ritual to awaken Zildrog was already underway. GEMINI 16 betrayed some of her allies, locking them inside energy transfer chambers to be used as fuel for Zildrog's awakening, and trapped Alliance members in a [[force field]]. Awakened after centuries of slumber, Zildrog demanded a target to feed on, and GEMINI 16 enabled it to connect to the ''Gravestone'', parked on the Alliance capital of [[Odessen]].<ref name="Nathema" />

[[File:Zildrog_and_Vinn_Atrius.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Zildrog empowers Vinn Atrius.]]
Controlling the vessel through the Dark Sanctuary, Zildrog took the ''Gravestone'' into Odessen's orbit and proceeded to repeatedly fire the omnicannon at the Eternal Fleet. After the Fleet was completely obliterated, Zildrog targeted Odessen itself but required to gather power before the next attack. This resulted in dropping the force field that kept the Alliance members on Nathema restrained, allowing them to engage GEMINI 16. They fought and destroyed the droid, but before they could shut Zildrog down, Vinn Atrius ordered Zildrog to enhance him with its power. Augmented with increased strength, Atrius attacked the Alliance while Zildrog encouraged his new servant to destroy their enemies. However, the Commander and Beniko defeated Atrius and destroyed Zildrog, which also triggered the [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]] of the ''Gravestone''. The warship exploded over Odessen, bringing an end to the era in which Iokath weapons affected the fate of the entire galaxy.<ref name="Nathema" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Zildrog_concept_art.jpg|thumb|250px|Concept art of Zildrog]]Zildrog was introduced in the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire|''Knights of the Fallen Empire'']] expansion of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' as a [[Deity/Legends|deity]] worshipped by the ancient people of [[Zakuul]] and modern fringe cultists.<ref name="KOTFE 4" /> Zildrog later appeared as the last boss of "The Nathema Conspiracy" flashpoint, released during the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|''Knights of the Eternal Throne'']] expansion cycle, which revealed that it was in fact a sentient [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] that originated on [[Iokath]].<ref name="Nathema" />

During the flashpoint Zildrog claims that he was the one responsible for the [[Ritual of Nathema]], which caused confusion among players, as the ritual was previously believed to be performed solely by [[Tenebrae|Vitiate]]. Writer [[Charles Boyd]] clarified the issue by highlighting player posts which noted that the [[Sith Emperor's ritual]] always required a mass death to be triggered by an outside source before Vitiate could use the life essences of the dead to empower himself, and adding "y'all have it pretty much sorted here".<ref name="TORweb-Charles Boyd on Forums: Was Vitiate a fraud then? Confused about a line from the FP spoilers obviously">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=9593256|text=Charles Boyd on Forums: "Was Vitiate a fraud then? Confused about a line from the FP (spoilers obviously)"}}</ref>
